title: All four Work Orders settings ask you to confirm before they save
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner or Admin.

2. Open the Work Orders settings page: in the left sidebar under SETTINGS click "Settings", then the "Work Orders" tab at the top of the page - the page with the WORKFLOW, LINE REQUIREMENTS and PARTS groups and a "Save Settings" button.

3. Have some open work orders carrying parts, so that each setting has a non-zero number of records to report. For example the work orders listed under "Work Orders" -> the "Work Orders" tab.
custom_steps:
1. Switch "Require Ordering Parts" and read the confirmation that opens. Press Cancel.

2. Switch "Require Picking Inventory Parts" and read the confirmation that opens. Press Cancel.

3. Switch "Require Approval for New Lines" and read the confirmation that opens. Press Cancel.

4. Switch "Require Receiving Parts Before Completion" and read the confirmation that opens. Press Cancel.

5. For each of the four, check that the confirmation names the setting, says which way it is going, and gives a count of the records the requirement affects at this location today.
custom_expected:
1. All four settings on the Work Orders settings page ask you to confirm before anything is saved - Require Ordering Parts, Require Picking Inventory Parts, Require Approval for New Lines and Require Receiving Parts Before Completion. None of them saves silently.

2. Each confirmation names the setting and the direction it is going, for example "Turn on Require Ordering Parts?" or "Turn off Require Receiving Parts Before Completion?"

3. Each one says in plain words what the setting will mean from now on, and gives a live count of what the requirement affects at this location today - parts, lines or work orders, whichever the setting governs.

4. Each one states that switching it changes nothing that already exists: "No record is changed by this switch. Parts already on a work order keep the state they are in." For the approval setting the same is said of lines.

5. Each one offers Cancel and a button naming the direction - "Turn On" or "Turn Off". Nothing is saved until that button and then "Save Settings" are pressed.

Source:

  • QA lead ruling, 25 September 2026 - asking to confirm on all four settings is the expected behaviour, and the confirmation's own words are what the product is meant to say: "No record is changed by this switch. Parts already on a work order keep the state they are in."
  • Epic SV-8683, story SV-9249 (Story 3, Confirmation before a settings change), Simple Flow V2 specification (Confluence page 771391574).

Last checked against build v26.39.0-07c719b on 9/25/2026.
